stem: Why is screening or panel testing for food allergies discouraged in patients with no history of reactions?

options.text: It can lead to false positive results and unnecessary food restrictions.
The tests are too expensive to be performed without a documented emergency.
It increases the risk of the patient developing a new allergy through the testing process.
Skin prick testing cannot be performed on patients who have never eaten the food.

explanation: Approximately $30-50\%$ of children may show sensitivity on tests despite being able to tolerate the food clinically.
rationale: Consider the high percentage of people who have positive tests but can actually eat the food.

optionExplanations.A: Approximately $30-50\%$ of children may show sensitivity on tests despite being able to tolerate the food clinically.
optionExplanations.B: The primary concern is clinical accuracy and patient well-being rather than the financial cost of the test.
optionExplanations.C: Testing itself does not cause the development of allergies; the risk lies in the misinterpretation of results.
optionExplanations.D: The test can be performed, but it lacks clinical utility without a history to correlate with the results.

source.hint: Consider the high percentage of people who have positive tests but can actually eat the food.
